questions.explanationText: 'whereas' is correct because whereas contrasts the two options. The other choices express a different logical relationship.

questions.questionText:
The training includes simulated emergencies so that employees can practise decisions under pressure. _____ a real incident occurs, they should respond more confidently.

Choose the option that best preserves the intended meaning.
questions.explanationText: 'When' is correct because when introduces the future situation for which training prepares them. The other choices express a different logical relationship.

questions.questionText:
A hospital introduced an AI tool to prioritise scans. During the pilot, doctors reviewed every recommendation rather than accepting it automatically. They discovered that the tool performed less accurately on images from one older scanner. The hospital paused wider deployment until the cause was understood. This response was appropriately _____.

Choose the most appropriate word or phrase to complete the sentence.
questions.explanationText: 'cautious' best fits because pausing after discovering uneven performance shows justified caution. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
A manufacturer tracked defects only at the final inspection stage. By then, faulty batches had already consumed materials and machine time. The company began monitoring each production stage instead. Problems could then be corrected soon after they appeared, making the process more _____.

Select the option that best fits the blank.
questions.explanationText: 'efficient' best fits because early correction reduces wasted material and time. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
A city planted thousands of trees but initially gave little attention to maintenance. Many young trees died during the first dry season. The next programme included watering schedules, local caretakers, and survival audits. The city had learned that planting targets alone were _____.

Which option best completes the sentence or passage?
questions.explanationText: 'insufficient' best fits because successful outcomes also require maintenance and monitoring. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
An online retailer measured support agents only by the number of calls completed. Agents rushed conversations, and repeat calls increased. The company added measures of resolution quality and customer satisfaction. The revised system offered a more _____ view of performance.

Identify the word or phrase that makes the text grammatically and contextually correct.
questions.explanationText: 'comprehensive' best fits because multiple quality and satisfaction measures create a broader assessment. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
A university wanted to reduce laboratory accidents. It first sent a general safety email, but behaviour barely changed. It then introduced practical demonstrations, short quizzes, and supervisor observations. Incident rates fell. The later approach was more _____.

Choose the best contextual fit.
questions.explanationText: 'engaging' best fits because demonstrations and quizzes involve participants actively. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
A farming cooperative installed soil sensors across several fields. Readings from two locations were consistently unusual, but technicians found those sensors beside irrigation outlets. The cooperative moved them to typical field locations before using the data. This improved the sample's _____.

Which option should replace the blank?
questions.explanationText: 'representativeness' best fits because typical locations make readings more representative of whole fields. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
A transport company promised faster deliveries and added more vehicles. Congestion, not vehicle shortage, was the main cause of delay. After analysing routes, it shifted departures and consolidated nearby stops. The example shows why solutions should target the _____ cause of a problem.

Select the most suitable expression.
questions.explanationText: 'underlying' best fits because route analysis identified the fundamental source rather than a surface symptom. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
An employee survey showed low morale, and managers immediately planned a social event. Follow-up interviews revealed that unclear promotion criteria were the real concern. Management then published standards and created an appeal process. The interviews provided essential _____.

Choose the option that best preserves the intended meaning.
questions.explanationText: 'context' best fits because interviews explained what lay behind the survey result. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
A coastal community built a barrier against storm surges. Engineers also restored wetlands, updated evacuation routes, and improved warning systems. They recognised that no single measure could remove all risk. Their strategy was therefore _____.

Choose the most appropriate word or phrase to complete the sentence.
questions.explanationText: 'multifaceted' best fits because the strategy combines several distinct protective measures. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
A research team obtained a striking result from a small sample. Rather than announcing a breakthrough, it shared the method and invited other laboratories to repeat the study. Independent confirmation would make the finding more _____.

Select the option that best fits the blank.
questions.explanationText: 'credible' best fits because successful independent repetition increases trustworthiness. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
The auditor described the missing receipt as a minor _____ that did not alter the overall conclusion.

Which option best completes the sentence or passage?
questions.explanationText: 'discrepancy' best fits because discrepancy is a small inconsistency in records. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
The spokesperson's answer was deliberately _____, avoiding a firm commitment while negotiations continued.

Identify the word or phrase that makes the text grammatically and contextually correct.
questions.explanationText: 'noncommittal' best fits because avoiding commitment is noncommittal. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
The evidence is _____ with the engineer's explanation, though it does not prove it conclusively.

Choose the best contextual fit.
questions.explanationText: 'consistent' best fits because consistent with means compatible with the explanation. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
The new rule may _____ innovation if compliance becomes unnecessarily expensive.

Which option should replace the blank?
questions.explanationText: 'inhibit' best fits because high compliance costs can restrain innovation. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
Because the proposal relied on several untested assumptions, the panel considered it _____.

Select the most suitable expression.
questions.explanationText: 'speculative' best fits because untested assumptions make a proposal conjectural. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
The revised estimate is more _____ because it includes maintenance and training costs.

Choose the option that best preserves the intended meaning.
questions.explanationText: 'realistic' best fits because including omitted costs makes the estimate closer to reality. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
The lawyer used _____ language so that the agreement could not be interpreted in two ways.

Choose the most appropriate word or phrase to complete the sentence.
questions.explanationText: 'unambiguous' best fits because avoiding two interpretations requires unambiguous wording. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
The chief scientist remained _____ about the claim until the full data set was released.

Select the option that best fits the blank.
questions.explanationText: 'sceptical' best fits because withholding belief pending data is scepticism. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
The committee reached a _____ decision after members with conflicts of interest withdrew.

Which option best completes the sentence or passage?
questions.explanationText: 'impartial' best fits because removing conflicts supports fairness and impartiality. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
The benefits were _____ across departments: some saved hours each week, while others saw little change.

Identify the word or phrase that makes the text grammatically and contextually correct.
questions.explanationText: 'uneven' best fits because different levels of benefit indicate uneven distribution. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
The regulator asked the bank to _____ the suspicious transactions in greater detail.

Choose the best contextual fit.
questions.explanationText: 'look into' best fits because look into means investigate. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
The meeting was _____ until the missing safety report became available.

Which option should replace the blank?
questions.explanationText: 'put off' best fits because put off means postponed. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
Even during the outage, the backup team managed to _____ essential services.

Select the most suitable expression.
questions.explanationText: 'keep up' best fits because keep up means maintain services. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
The new manager quickly _____ a plan to reduce repeated approval steps.

Choose the option that best preserves the intended meaning.
questions.explanationText: 'came up with' best fits because come up with means devise an idea or plan. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
We need to _____ why the test results differ before repeating the experiment.

Choose the most appropriate word or phrase to complete the sentence.
questions.explanationText: 'figure out' best fits because figure out means understand or solve. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
The supplier promised to _____ the faulty units at no additional cost.

Select the option that best fits the blank.
questions.explanationText: 'replace' best fits because replace directly takes the object being removed. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
The project was delayed because two contractors _____ of the agreement unexpectedly.

Which option best completes the sentence or passage?
questions.explanationText: 'backed out' best fits because back out of means withdraw from a commitment. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
The team decided to _____ the old database gradually rather than shut it down at once.

Identify the word or phrase that makes the text grammatically and contextually correct.
questions.explanationText: 'phase out' best fits because phase out means discontinue in stages. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
Please _____ the main findings in your own words at the end of the presentation.

Choose the best contextual fit.
questions.explanationText: 'sum up' best fits because sum up means give a concise summary. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
The engineers had to _____ a temporary solution until the replacement part arrived.

Which option should replace the blank?
questions.explanationText: 'devise' best fits because devise means create a practical plan or method. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
Only _____ applicants had experience with both hardware and embedded software.

Select the most suitable expression.
questions.explanationText: 'a few' is correct because a few modifies the countable plural noun applicants; it makes the completed sentence grammatically natural.

questions.questionText:
There is _____ time left, so we should focus on the most important tests.

Choose the option that best preserves the intended meaning.
questions.explanationText: 'little' is correct because little modifies the uncountable noun time and indicates scarcity; it makes the completed sentence grammatically natural.

questions.questionText:
The revised process produced _____ errors than the manual one.

Choose the most appropriate word or phrase to complete the sentence.
questions.explanationText: 'fewer' is correct because fewer is used with countable plural errors; it makes the completed sentence grammatically natural.

questions.questionText:
This sensor is _____ accurate than the older model under low-light conditions.

Select the option that best fits the blank.
questions.explanationText: 'more' is correct because more forms the comparative of accurate; it makes the completed sentence grammatically natural.

questions.questionText:
Of the four routes, the coastal road is the _____.

Which option best completes the sentence or passage?
questions.explanationText: 'shortest' is correct because the superlative is required when comparing four routes; it makes the completed sentence grammatically natural.

questions.questionText:
Neither of the proposed dates _____ suitable for all participants.

Identify the word or phrase that makes the text grammatically and contextually correct.
questions.explanationText: 'is' is correct because neither is singular in formal agreement; it makes the completed sentence grammatically natural.

questions.questionText:
We have received _____ information to begin the preliminary assessment.

Choose the best contextual fit.
questions.explanationText: 'enough' is correct because enough correctly modifies the uncountable noun information; it makes the completed sentence grammatically natural.

questions.questionText:
The second prototype consumed _____ than half the power used by the first.

Which option should replace the blank?
questions.explanationText: 'less' is correct because less is used for an amount of power; it makes the completed sentence grammatically natural.

questions.questionText:
There were too _____ chairs for everyone to sit during the briefing.

Select the most suitable expression.
questions.explanationText: 'few' is correct because few modifies countable plural chairs; it makes the completed sentence grammatically natural.

questions.questionText:
_____ solution addresses both the cost problem and the safety risk.

Choose the option that best preserves the intended meaning.
questions.explanationText: 'Neither' is correct because neither can directly determine a singular noun and means not one of two; it makes the completed sentence grammatically natural.

questions.questionText:
Given the limited sample and short trial period, the report reaches a _____ conclusion rather than claiming certainty.

Choose the most appropriate word or phrase to complete the sentence.
questions.explanationText: 'tentative' best fits because limited evidence calls for a provisional conclusion. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
The notice asks residents to reduce water use and adopts an urgent but not _____ tone.

Select the option that best fits the blank.
questions.explanationText: 'alarmist' best fits because the message is urgent without exaggerating danger. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
The review acknowledges the product's useful features but remains _____ of its poor accessibility.

Which option best completes the sentence or passage?
questions.explanationText: 'critical' best fits because acknowledging strengths while noting a serious weakness is critical. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
Because the recovery exceeded every forecast, the directors were _____ about the next quarter.

Identify the word or phrase that makes the text grammatically and contextually correct.
questions.explanationText: 'optimistic' best fits because better-than-expected recovery supports positive expectations. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
The scientist's statement was deliberately _____: she said the treatment might help but required further study.

Choose the best contextual fit.
questions.explanationText: 'measured' best fits because qualified language and a call for study create a measured tone. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
The farewell message was warm and _____, thanking colleagues for years of support.

Which option should replace the blank?
questions.explanationText: 'appreciative' best fits because thanks for support convey appreciation. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
The regulator's response was _____, stating facts without praising or condemning the company.

Select the most suitable expression.
questions.explanationText: 'neutral' best fits because fact-based language without judgment is neutral. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
The proposal uses evidence and clear benefits to adopt a _____ tone.

Choose the option that best preserves the intended meaning.
questions.explanationText: 'persuasive' best fits because evidence and benefits are used to convince the reader. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
The author treats the claim with _____, questioning both its data and its assumptions.

Choose the most appropriate word or phrase to complete the sentence.
questions.explanationText: 'scepticism' best fits because questioning evidence and assumptions demonstrates scepticism. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
The update reassured customers without minimising the incident, creating a calm and _____ tone.

Select the option that best fits the blank.
questions.explanationText: 'responsible' best fits because acknowledgment plus reassurance is responsible communication. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
The two indicators often move together, but this relationship should not be _____ as proof that one causes the other.

Which option best completes the sentence or passage?
questions.explanationText: 'interpreted' best fits because correlation must not be treated as causal proof. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
Although the policy is uniform on paper, its impact may be _____ because departments have different resources.

Identify the word or phrase that makes the text grammatically and contextually correct.
questions.explanationText: 'variable' best fits because different resources can produce varying effects. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
The consultant's recommendation was _____ on the assumption that demand would remain stable.

Choose the best contextual fit.
questions.explanationText: 'contingent' best fits because contingent on means dependent on a condition. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
A technically accurate answer may still be _____ if it does not address the question the client actually asked.

Which option should replace the blank?
questions.explanationText: 'irrelevant' best fits because accuracy does not create relevance to a different question. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
The pilot was small enough to limit financial risk yet large enough to produce _____ operational evidence.

Select the most suitable expression.
questions.explanationText: 'meaningful' best fits because the scale was chosen to yield useful real-world evidence. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
The absence of complaints cannot be taken as _____ evidence of satisfaction because many users simply leave.

Choose the option that best preserves the intended meaning.
questions.explanationText: 'conclusive' best fits because silent departures prevent the evidence from proving satisfaction. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
The system's apparent simplicity is _____; substantial processing occurs behind the interface.

Choose the most appropriate word or phrase to complete the sentence.
questions.explanationText: 'deceptive' best fits because the simple appearance hides underlying complexity. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
The board accepted a slower rollout as a reasonable _____ between speed and reliability.

Select the option that best fits the blank.
questions.explanationText: 'trade-off' best fits because a trade-off balances competing advantages. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
The model performed well on familiar cases but failed when conditions changed, revealing limited _____.

Which option best completes the sentence or passage?
questions.explanationText: 'generalisability' best fits because failure in new conditions shows limited ability to generalise. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.

questions.questionText:
By publishing both favourable and unfavourable results, the team reduced the risk of _____ bias.

Identify the word or phrase that makes the text grammatically and contextually correct.
questions.explanationText: 'selective-reporting' best fits because reporting all outcomes reduces selective-reporting bias. The other options conflict with the surrounding meaning or usage.
